clue.text: Who's set to deal with paw on leg?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a leg of a journey or tour is a stage
a paw is a hand, informally

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a dog that keeps putting its paw on someone's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'set': a stagehand deals with the scenery sets in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre worker whose job is moving and handling the scenery, the sets, during a production.

clue.text: Short of time, son chucked difficult woman

indicators.note: short of means lacking this letter

parts.note: chucked means threw

explanation.surface: Running out of time, a son walked out on a demanding woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging woman, as in The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Close to new wedding place shortly to go up in old Olympic venue

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the pieces backwards

parts.note: at means near or close to a place

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an altar is where a church wedding takes place

explanation.surface: A new church wedding venue shortly to rise near a former Olympic site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to new' looks like the last letter of new, but it is AT plus N; all pieces are then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta, Georgia, hosted the 1996 Summer Olympic Games, so it is a past Olympic city.

clue.text: Heat in blaze warped type of period architecture

indicators.note: warped means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heat from a fire has bent the timbers of an old building of a historic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabethan describes the late-Tudor building style of Elizabeth I's reign, often half-timbered.

clue.text: Sore area initially goes round part of face

indicators.note: goes round means these letters surround another piece
initially means taking the first letters of the words either side

parts.note: the chin is part of the face

explanation.surface: A sore patch at first spreads round part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Aching means hurting with a dull pain, which is what being sore is.

clue.text: Ailment or side treated with doctor doing rounds?

indicators.note: doing rounds means going round, so this piece encloses the other
treated means processed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital picture: an illness or a pain in the side treated by a doctor on his rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the doctor 'doing rounds': on the ward he goes round patients, here round letters that 'treated' has rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder is an illness or medical condition, as in a stomach disorder.

clue.text: Regressing predictably features this drink …

indicators.note: regressing means going backwards, so the run is read from right to left
the word predictably features, that is contains, a run of letters

explanation.surface: A remark that heavy drinking predictably brings on relapse, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints LIDER, not a word; the wordplay plainly gives CIDER, and 6 down's first letter, shared with this entry, is the C of CAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apples, so it fits a clue asking for a drink.

clue.text: What may be seen primarily in cycle-and bus-lanes?

definitions.text: What may be seen primarily in cycle-and bus-lanes?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A question about what traffic one expects to see in the reserved lanes of a city street.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints LAB, but the initials give CAB, which also crosses the C of 6 across. A taxi may use a bus lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxis are permitted in many bus lanes, so a cab is a vehicle seen there.

clue.text: Surrey town men separating duke and monarch

indicators.note: separating means coming between the two pieces

parts.note: a king is a monarch
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, men

explanation.surface: Some men coming between a duke and the king in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London; Dorking is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorking is a market town in the county of Surrey in south-east England.

clue.text: What's made early, simply to be cooked?

definitions.text: What's made early, simply to be cooked?

indicators.note: to be cooked means the letters are to be prepared again, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about a dish prepared ahead that just needs heating.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a ready meal is made in advance and only needs simple heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready meal is a pre-prepared supermarket dish made in advance that simply needs heating.

clue.text: … almost fitting to swallow another 3 favoured by queen

indicators.note: to swallow means one piece goes inside the other
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: fitting, as in proper, means right
following on from the previous clue's drink, another drink here is ale

explanation.surface: A continuation of the drink clue: something nearly suitable taking in another drink, liked by royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to 3 down: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan courtier famously favoured by Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Raleigh was a courtier and explorer of Elizabeth I's reign, one of the queen's favourites.

clue.text: After revolution, song is about to represent part of Russia

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the little word is reversed

parts.note: to represent someone is to be them, as an actor might

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the word for song is reversed

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A political picture: after the revolution, a song stands for a Russian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After revolution' sounds like Russian history, but it only says the song is turned round; 'about' likewise turns 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast northern Asian region of the Russian Federation.

clue.text: Red possibly not quite completing triumph

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: red is one example of wine, hence 'possibly'

explanation.surface: A glass of red not quite finished when celebrating a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph over something is to win, a direct synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Anomaly with Brit intermittently involved is still a deviation

indicators.note: involved means mixed up together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that an oddity mixed up with a British person is still out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' suggests picking alternate letters, but all of ANOMALY and BRIT are needed: eleven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: An abnormality is a departure from what is normal, that is a deviation from the standard.

clue.text: Good news of whole family's health, as it may be

definitions.text: Good news of whole family's health
definitions.meaning: everybody being healthy, every member fine
the phrase said grudgingly, conceding a point before a but

explanation.surface: Two readings of a phrase: the family are all healthy, or a grudging concession.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'that's fine as far as it goes' is a grudging concession, while literally everyone being healthy is good family news.

clue.text: Descendants burying sailor in Davy Jones's locker

indicators.note: burying means holding one piece inside the other

parts.note: seed, in the biblical sense, means offspring or descendants
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Heirs burying a seaman at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Davy Jones's locker is the sailors' name for the bottom of the sea, where the drowned lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Davy Jones's locker is seafaring slang for the ocean floor, the grave of drowned sailors.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic concentrate which can hide signs of age?

definitions.text: which can hide signs of age?

parts.note: a soft drink is one without alcohol
to focus is to concentrate

explanation.surface: Drinking soft drinks and concentrating as a way to look younger.
explanation.walkthrough: Soft focus is a photographic technique blurring the image slightly, flattering wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly blurred photography softens wrinkles and blemishes, so it can disguise how old someone looks.

clue.text: Society's put off from seeing leg flexed in filmy robe

indicators.note: flexed means bent, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A society put off by the sight of a bent leg in a flimsy dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off from' removes the S of SEEING, leaving EEING; with LEG, 'flexed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, often sheer dressing gown worn by women, a filmy robe.

clue.text: Remote chance unmatched in desires

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to long for is to desire, so desires means longs
odd means not part of a matching pair, as an odd sock

explanation.surface: Unrequited longing, with little hope of success.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting terms, high odds against something mean it is unlikely: a slim prospect.

clue.text: Loose mass seizing quiet moment — to perform a prearranged public act?

definitions.text: to perform a prearranged public act?

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: flab is loose, flabby body tissue
SH is the call for quiet
a mo is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: A crowd taking a quiet moment before staging a planned public stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: A flash mob is a crowd gathered, by plan, to perform something briefly in public; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash mob is a group who assemble suddenly in a public place to perform a pre-planned act.

clue.text: Cost of travelling over a long distance is shortly made known

indicators.note: over here means spreading across, so one piece covers the other
shortly means cut short by the last letter

parts.note: to air a view is to make it known, so made known is aired
far means a long way off

explanation.surface: The price of a long journey being announced briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfare is the price paid for a flight, a cost of travelling by plane.

clue.text: Solution for dried-up writer conversely left one with a long sentence

indicators.note: conversely means the other way round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence

explanation.surface: A writer with nothing left in them, set beside a long-term prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dried-up writer' is a pen out of ink, not an exhausted author.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen that has run dry is solved by a new ink cartridge or tube put in it.

clue.text: Paper's edges covered by one pristine stamp

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: covered by means sitting inside another piece

parts.note: mint, as in mint condition, means pristine

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A philatelist's picture: a mint stamp with its paper edges protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper's edges' gives P and R, which go inside MINT.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a mark pressed into a surface, and to stamp is to make such a mark.

clue.text: Current collection of papers kept under stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, kept under means placed below the other piece

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
a ream is a bundle of 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A pile of documents weighted down by a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flow of water, and a current is a flow in a particular direction.

clue.text: Float around back of planet Mercury and start reversing at regular intervals

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: to fly is to float through the air

indicators.note: reversing means these pieces are read backwards
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
an intro is a start or opening

explanation.surface: An astronomical image: drifting round the planet Mercury and turning back periodically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planet Mercury' reads as one phrase, but 'back of planet' is its last letter and Mercury is the element; 'reversing' turns those with 'start' before 'around' puts them inside the float.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening every two weeks occurs at a fixed recurring interval of a fortnight.

clue.text: Place to rest wickets after sport

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school sport
W is the cricket abbreviation for wickets

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: somewhere to sit after the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a bench seat in a church, somewhere to sit and rest.

clue.text: Early part of Bible penned by apparently weak God

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed inside another piece

parts.note: wan means pale and looking weak
OT, the Old Testament, is the earlier part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Scripture written by a deity who seems feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotan is the Germanic name for Odin, chief god of Norse and Germanic mythology.

clue.text: Perhaps staffed by men in need of moisturiser?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., supplied with chaps, that is men
skin that is cracked and sore from cold wind needs cream

explanation.surface: A men-only workplace whose staff all need hand cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapped skin is rough and cracked, which moisturising cream treats; the first sense is a whimsical made-up verb from chap.

clue.text: Sweet potato gets top sliced off

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a spud is a potato, informally

explanation.surface: A potato with its top cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pud is British slang for pudding, which in Britain means any dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage pudding, shortened to pud, is the dessert course, a sweet.

clue.text: Member is entertained by Parisian and mournful writer

indicators.note: being entertained by means sitting inside the host piece

parts.note: et is French for and
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A member of a club hosted by a Parisian, who turns out to be a gloomy author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does two jobs only in appearance: it gives the letters IS, while 'entertained by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, sorrowful poems lamenting the dead, so is a mournful writer.

clue.text: Mount Cook? Did that in the past with wife absent

indicators.note: absent means this letter is removed

parts.words: Cook? Did that in the past
parts.note: to cook is to stew, and having done it is stewed

explanation.surface: Mount Cook in New Zealand, climbed long ago by someone whose wife stayed home.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Cook reads as the New Zealand peak, but the clue splits there: 'Mount' is the definition and 'Cook' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A steed is a horse for riding, and a mount is the animal one rides.

clue.text: Small mischief-maker revealed dope

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A naughty little child gives the game away about a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and a simpleton is a foolish one: synonyms.
